definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese percussion instrument made from a wooden body with animal skin stretched over both ends. Used in festivals, shrine rituals, performing arts, and modern ensemble performances. Composed of 和 (Japanese) + 太鼓 (drum).

examples.japanese: {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{響|ひび}いた→響く：00099_hibiku⟧。
examples.english: The sound of the Japanese drum echoed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{演奏|えんそう}→演奏：01896_ensou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聴|き}いた→聴く：30010_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I listened to a taiko performance at the festival.

examples.japanese: {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全身|ぜんしん}→全身：03313_zenshin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{体力|たいりょく}→体力：05318_tairyoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: Playing taiko requires physical strength since you use your whole body.

notes:
USAGE:
{和太鼓|わだいこ} distinguishes Japanese drums from Western drums (⟦ドラム→ドラム：04463_doramu⟧). In casual speech, ⟦{太鼓|たいこ}→太鼓：04049_taiko⟧ alone often refers to Japanese drums when the context is clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ / ⟦{叩|たた}く→叩く：02072_tataku⟧ (to play/beat a taiko)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{演奏|えんそう}→演奏：01896_ensou⟧ (taiko performance)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦グループ→グループ：03840_guruupu⟧ (taiko group/ensemble)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}⟦{体験|たいけん}→体験：11443_taiken⟧ (taiko experience/workshop)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{和太鼓|わだいこ} performance has evolved from traditional festival music into a modern performing art. Groups like {鼓童|こどう} have brought {和太鼓|わだいこ} to international audiences. Ensemble taiko ({組太鼓|くみだいこ}) as a stage art form developed primarily in the postwar period.
